items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1958-06-09
items.q: And he used Lloyd Kenner and Tom Brown as arch conspirators to say things that were untrue.

ctx.x: Fletcher Henderson and Benny Morton of Kansas City were also among the first swing artists. Benny Morton's name is spelled M-O-R-T-O-N. Do you want me to read the letter to the editor? Just a moment.

These Negroes showed their appreciation after I had made it easy for them to come up and open his publishing concern. He didn't know me. That 20 years had passed. In 1936, Lou Gensler had a big broadcast. He tried to locate us to put us in the beginning and Benny Goodman as the end. In other words, the beginning and end. At this time, all these prophets got up in arms against us. John Hammond was one of them. He worked for Handy, I suppose, some kind of cheap lawyer or something on that order. And Handy was given…

items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: The band consisted of Billy Lambard drums, Gus Miller clarinet, Raymond Lopez cornet, this fellow Lloyd Canna, Arnold Lloyd Canna, guitar, and Theo Brown bass.

ctx.x: I read a better letter where you asked him if you wanted to meet him before the jazz club. Oh yeah. Well I'll get to that. I understand.

And he's got me all mixed up now this guy. That's all right. And see stop it. When Brown went to Chicago the members of his band was not as he gives them in the later part of his band. The band consisted of Billy Lambard drums, Gus Miller clarinet, Raymond Lopez cornet, this fellow Lloyd Canna, Arnold Lloyd Canna, guitar, and Theo Brown bass. It's like Canna says he had taken music by some professor who learned more than one lesson than the kids learned in three years today. Well to tell you the truth I don't…
So now how did this trombone play as different say from Edwards?
